grammar.title: Of course with 当然
grammar.pattern: (主语) + 当然 + 动词/形容词短语
grammar.explanation: 当然 (dāngrán) means "of course, naturally" — used to confirm something is obviously true or to agree enthusiastically. It usually goes right before the verb or adjective, and can also stand alone as a reply meaning "Of course!".

grammar.title: The 所 nominalizer in formal writing
grammar.pattern: (主语) + 所 + 动词 + 的 + 名词
grammar.explanation: 所 (suǒ) can go right before a verb in formal or written Chinese, turning the verb phrase into something like "what/that which [subject] verbs". It's most often followed by 的 and a noun, and mainly used with two-syllable verbs like 说, 做, 想, 知道.

sentences.zh: 只有身体健康，才能好好工作。
sentences.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu shēntǐ jiànkāng, cái néng hǎohāo gōngzuò.
sentences.en: Only with good health can one work well.

sentences.pinyin: Tā céngjīng shì yī míng lǎoshī.

sentences.en: What exactly do you want to say?

sentences.pinyin: Zhè dàodǐ shì zěnme huí shì?
sentences.en: What on earth is going on here?
Are you going or not, after all?
